rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6 describe a one-season (2002) split-plot field experiment at PAU Regional Station Bathinda, India, with three replications. Q2: Section 3.1 and Table 4 report that drip at the same water and N (D0.4N100) gave 2144 kg/ha seed cotton versus 1624 kg/ha under check-basin (a 32% increase); drip at 75% water still gave 12% more yield; Conclusions restate the 32% yield gain.
rows.notes: The passage attributes the finding to Ad El-wahed & Ali (2013) on maize under sprinkler vs drip in Egypt; this study is cotton under drip vs check-basin in India, so the citation appears misattributed, though the technology (drip) and effect (crop yield) match generically. Q3: yield measured by one method (plot harvest) only. Q4: yield components (bolls/plant, seed cotton:stick ratio, stick biomass) and seasonal profile water are reported but the mechanism (better soil water availability under drip) is asserted by citing Mateos et al., not measured; rated no. Q5/Q6: one site, one soil, one crop, one season, plot scale. Q7: yield advantage is found to vary with water and N level (drip at 50% water gave 2% lower yield than check-basin), but authors do not state these as requirements. Q8: no explicit limitations beyond 'under these experimental conditions'. Q9: only LSD at 5% reported, no SD/SE/CI.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6 describe a replicated field experiment in Bathinda, India, summer 2002. Q2: Table 6 and Section 3.2 report measured irrigation water (54.6 cm check-basin vs 41.1 and 27.2 cm for drip at 0.3 and 0.2 Epan; 27.3 cm for paired-sown drip at 0.4 Epan) and WUE rising from 17.6 to 22.1 kg/ha cm (26%) under drip at the same water; Section 3.1 states drip at 75% water still yielded 12% more than check-basin, and paired-sown drip gave 20% more yield with 50% water saving; Conclusions restate 50-75% water saving under drip with paired sowing.
rows.notes: Passage names Ad El-wahed & Ali (2013), maize, sprinkler comparator, Egypt; this study is cotton, check-basin comparator, India <U+2014> apparent misattribution, but drip and water saving/water productivity match. Q3: water use measured by one approach (applied volume plus gravimetric profile water plus rainfall). Q4: no measurement of percolation, evaporation or soil water dynamics explaining the saving; mechanism not measured. Q5/Q6: single site, soil, crop, season, plot scale. Q7: water saving with paired sowing is attributed to one lateral per two rows (a design feature), and yield loss at 50% water/reduced N is a found variation, not stated as a requirement. Q8: no limitations stated on the result. Q9: no dispersion measures; only LSD values for yield.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a single-season field trial of drip vs check-basin irrigation in cotton with water, N and planting-pattern treatments; the review passage describes a different study (maize, sprinkler vs drip, Egypt), so the citation to this study looks like a mismatch in the review, but the study does contain its own evidence on drip yield gain and water saving.
